title: One Fox. Four Ways to See a Walk.

chapters.title: Start with the actual character
narrationParts: Meet the supplied Mesh2Motion fox, with forty-nine bones and fourteen animation clips.
We're inspecting its walk, not creating a new rig.

chapters.title: Four views, one walk
narrationParts: One moment, four useful views: surface, mesh, skeleton, and side profile.
They show the same walk, each revealing something different.

chapters.title: Follow the bend
chapters.body: Compare the same pose across all four panels.
narrationParts: Now slow the walk and follow how the legs bend.
Watch the same pose across all four views before judging it.

chapters.title: Hold a useful moment
chapters.body: Pose freezes at 24 seconds; playback resumes at 28.
narrationParts: Pause here, and compare the pose in each panel.
Then let the walk resume, keeping your eye on the changing silhouette.

chapters.title: Surface and structure
chapters.body: Use the mesh and skeleton to inspect the visible bend.
narrationParts: The mesh shows the surface structure; the skeleton shows the moving joints.
Use both to spot bends that deserve a closer look.

chapters.title: Review the whole cycle
chapters.body: Check awkward bends, clipping and the return to the first pose.
narrationParts: Before a longer video, check the full cycle for awkward bends and clipping.
Four views help inspection; they don't guarantee perfect animation.
